activity_statements.statement: designs and sells high-performance CPUs (EPYC server processors, Ryzen desktop/laptop) for data centers, AI workloads, and consumer PCs
designs and sells GPUs (Radeon, Instinct series) for graphics, gaming, and AI/machine learning acceleration in data centers
designs and sells FPGAs and adaptive computing solutions for intelligent edge devices and embedded applications
generates $34.6B in annual revenue as a fabless semiconductor company that designs chips and outsources fabrication to foundries
competes for data center AI accelerator market share against Nvidia with the Instinct MI-series GPU line

name_reality_gap: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) sounds generic; it is actually the primary challenger to Intel in CPUs and to Nvidia in AI/data-center GPUs. The company is a pure design house (fabless) — it does not own or operate semiconductor fabrication plants, which is invisible from the 'manufacturing' industry label assigned by the index.
extraction_notes: AMD's own website timed out repeatedly; data sourced from Exa company profile (LinkedIn-sourced data). Revenue of $34.6B and product line confirmed from this source. Segment weights estimated from publicly known AMD 2024 annual report structure, not directly retrieved.
